name: Nasty Green
lede: Nasty Green is a hard, slightly acid yellow-green, named by an online color survey with a word of dislike, and a reminder that painters were once scolded for the same color.

sections.title: A verdict as a name
sections.body:
The library records Nasty Green only from a 2010 crowd-sourced survey, and the nearest ISCC-NBS category is strong yellow green, about 8.3 units away [1]. Its nearest named relatives are [[grass]], [[kelly-green]] and [[apple-green]] [2].

The word has one earlier echo in the books. Ball reports that a Royal Academy member is said to have called one of Constable's landscapes a "nasty green thing", because Constable kept his greens fresher than the dark conventions of the day allowed [3]. Ball tells it as a reported remark, and nothing connects it to this swatch [3][4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Nasty Green appears in 3 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.01%, as photographed, which is rarer than 79% of the named colors [5]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole, and these are photographs of varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [5].
